paasCandidateExpiry.mechanism: scripts/close-expired-approvals.sh runs every 15 minutes and calls scripts/cleanup-candidate-tag.sh for an expired approval issue, deleting the -pending-approval candidate tag.

modelAcceptance.scope: Real conversations through the Web clients against the R4 canonical image fixture (agent-connect-qa). Pi via an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions gateway (endpoint and key not recorded). Claude not logged in; Codex ChatGPT account at its usage limit, so both are only used for AUTH-01. Smart sites were run on 0.17.4 and, after their redeploy, again on 0.17.5.
modelAcceptance.method: Random marker per reply; the daemon timeline must show the provider, the model and a NEW assistant message; the page is checked as well. MCP-01 verifies the product through the daemon and records page sync separately. Receipts keep booleans and stable codes only. Conversations are archived afterwards.

models.B: qa-gateway/nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning:free (tester-selected after nemotron-3-super-120b returned 404/429 from the gateway)

resultNotes.MODEL-03: The first Enter after a page reload was ignored on every client (reloadSendAttempts = 2); the second attempt succeeded.
resultNotes.MCP-01: Product behaviour (native-resume, same conversation id, history preserved, new tool called once) verified through the daemon on every client. The open page stayed in sync on official 0.17.6 and Woowtech 0.17.5 only in the final runs.
resultNotes.MCP-02: Busy refresh refused with SESSION_BUSY after the daemon confirmed the conversation was busy; permission-wait variant NOT verified (Pi has no permission prompts).
resultNotes.AUTH-01: Claude: PROVIDER_AUTH_REQUIRED, Codex: PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED, shown in the conversation and classified by the daemon; no success reply. Run on official 0.17.6 and Smart 0.17.5 only.

firstEnterAfterReload.observation: In the first MODEL-03 attempt the post-reload question never reached the daemon on 2 of 3 clients (no such user message in the daemon timeline); after waiting for the conversation to be restored and confirming acceptance, every client/version needed a second Enter.
firstEnterAfterReload.interpretation: Web client reconnect timing after a reload; not the daemon or this branch.

workingIndicatorAfterExternalMcpRefresh.observation: After a refresh triggered from another client, the first message sent immediately afterwards shows its reply but can leave the working indicator on until the page is reloaded; the daemon already holds the complete reply.
workingIndicatorAfterExternalMcpRefresh.abTestNote: Derived from private count-only debug logs (no text, offers or state); each run has a debug receipt in the evidence directory. refreshPath managed = this branch refreshMcp (managedMcpRefresh flag); upstream = Paseo refresh_agent_request without the flag. Waiting 12-15 s before sending avoided the stuck indicator in the recorded runs (1 official run at 12 s, 2 Apporo 0.17.5 runs at 15 s).
workingIndicatorAfterExternalMcpRefresh.interpretation: Not caused by the managed MCP patch: the upstream refresh path shows the same behaviour on Apporo 0.17.4 (3 of 3) and official 0.17.6 (1 of 1). Treated as Web client behaviour; mitigation is to wait or reload.

modelAcceptance.harnessNote: The QA harness sources live in the QA workspace, not in the product repositories. Attempts that failed for harness reasons are kept as receipts: piStopAndReloadFirstAttempt (reload send timing), piToolMcpFirstShakedown (tool-event check read the wrong field), piToolMcpSecondAttempt (MCP-01 could not observe a stale page), smart0175PiStopAndReloadFirstAttempt (browser timeout on reload) and smart0175PiToolMcpFirstAttempt (MCP-02: the model finished the turn with a shell loop before the refresh was attempted, so the daemon was idle; the harness now asks the daemon whether the conversation is busy before the refresh and retries with a fresh conversation).

cleanup.leftInPlace: archived test conversations/sessions created by the acceptance runs (no credentials)

realHostAcceptance.boundary: GitHub-hosted ephemeral runners; no company host was used or changed. HA OS ran as a QEMU/KVM VM on an x86_64 runner. The HA aarch64 run used the Store mock Supervisor, not a real Supervisor. No model calls or account logins.
realHostAcceptance.whyHostedRunners: Cluster storage was near its limits (Longhorn could schedule new volumes on one node only; node system disks had 18-32 GB free), so test VMs in the cluster would have risked PaaS volume provisioning.

podmanRepeatRun.why: Same scope as the canonical Podman run, all four jobs PASS. The canonical run repeated it only to keep redacted journal error samples in the receipts; this run recorded counts without samples.

podmanJournalErrorLines.onlySampledLine: [File Watcher (universal)] restarting watcher after unexpected error: terminated by itself with code null, signal: SIGTERM
podmanJournalErrorLines.meaning: User-journal lines containing "error" after the whole gate. The single sampled line is the VS Code file watcher inside code-server being terminated by SIGTERM when the first persistence case deliberately restarts the unit; the watcher restarts automatically. The canonical run had no other error lines; the repeat run counted one line in each amd64 job without keeping samples.

realHostAcceptance.legacyToR4DirectUpgrade: Paseo 0.11.2 (Podman main 4.139.1-9, HA 0.1.16) upgraded directly to R4 on native Podman (amd64, arm64) and real HAOS: same-browser workspace read before, identical server-id and keypair file hashes after, and the same browser read freshly written server bytes with no second offer. Earlier k3s receipts covered 0.11.2->R3 and R3->R4 only.
observations: HA Core 2026.11 under Supervisor defaults to HTTP port 80 (as on this fresh HAOS install); port 8123 is only a 307 redirect until onboarding completes (homeassistant/components/http/config.py, server.py). The add-on DOCS.md and README use http://<HA-IP>:8123 as the example of an HTTP LAN address not to use (the chat webview stays blank); the advice stands, only the example port is outdated for new installs.
Supervisor 2026.11 warns that the add-on config.yaml uses legacy map types 'addons' and 'all_addon_configs' (suggests 'local_apps' and 'all_app_configs'); it still works.
HAOS Docker uses the containerd image store: the container image ID is the manifest digest; it matched the candidate digest.

attempts.harnessIssue: README builds PASS on amd64/arm64; upgrades FAIL only legacy_daemon_paired_with_official_client: the harness required the legacy display name on screen before the upgrade, which the k3s migration receipt never required.

README builds PASS again; upgrades FAIL only legacy_browser_trust_survives_upgrade_without_new_offer: the harness looked for the host name text instead of reading the workspace; replaced by the k3s migration stages (identity files, same-browser fresh read).
HA_CORE_NOT_READY: the harness forwarded only guest port 8123; HA Core 2026.11 under Supervisor serves port 80.
Same as above, now with diagnostics: Core RUNNING inside the guest, front door not reachable.
FRONT_DOOR_UNREACHABLE_WHILE_CORE_UP: inside the guest port 8123 answered 307 to port 80; the forward was moved to guest port 80.
The Supervisor landing page answers 401 on port 80 while Core installs; the harness took 401 as ready and onboarding was refused.
RELEASED_IMAGE_MISMATCH: HAOS Docker uses the containerd image store, so the container image ID is the manifest digest, not the config digest.
Everything else PASS; the host-reboot case waited for the onboarding view, which HA removes once onboarding is complete (404).

stillNotCovered: install/update through the WOOW HA App Store

remainingGates: Model conversations: Pi was accepted on the official client (0.17.6) and on both Smart sites (0.17.4 and, after redeploy, 0.17.5): MODEL-01/02/03/04, TOOL-01/02, MCP-01/02; AUTH-01 on official and Smart 0.17.5. Claude and Codex positive paths remain unaccepted (Claude not logged in; the Codex ChatGPT account was at its usage limit). MCP-02 permission-wait variant is unverified (Pi has no permission prompts). Voice/microphone and agent-backed Tasks/schedule execution are not accepted.

Real hosts (2026-11-27 night, GitHub-hosted runners, no company host used): native rootless Podman + systemd/Quadlet on Ubuntu 24.04 (amd64 and physical arm64) passed both the README local build and the main 4.139.1-9 -> 4.139.1-10 upgrade; a real HA OS 18.3 VM (QEMU/KVM, Supervisor 2026.11.0, Core 2026.11.3) passed Supervisor install/update/restore/reinstall with the core suite, native panel through real HA login + Ingress and persistence including a host reboot; the HA aarch64 image passed on physical arm64 with the Store mock Supervisor. Not covered: physical HA hardware, arm64 HA OS, installation/update through the WOOW HA App Store (a local add-on with the same config.yaml and image was used), company-owned hosts, and the PaaS same-PVC upgrade.

Frontend cohorts: the R3 N-12 FAIL belonged to Smart 0.17.4, which lacked official 0.17.5 workspace selection. Smart was redeployed as 0.17.5 on 2026-11-27 (~15:00 Taipei) and N-12 passes in the R4 rerun; that deployment was not done by this runtime branch and is not a fix by it. N-13 (needs an existing agent) is still unverified on all clients.

PaaS R4 was tested with fresh PVCs while its candidate existed; a PaaS same-PVC image upgrade was not run and cannot run until the candidate is rebuilt. The separate canonical R3-to-R4 preserving image upgrade passed.
Standalone k3s/PaaS source contexts match across 631 tracked file modes and contents; no additional standalone k3s artifact was built or published.

No merge, Release, existing tenant rollout or stable/default chart image promotion. The PaaS candidate was removed when approval issue #808 expired (11-27 04:00Z); promotion would need a re-pushed tag and a new human approval.

Official Paseo web moved to 0.17.6 on 2026-11-27 and the Smart sites to 0.17.5 (~15:00 Taipei); earlier R3/R4 results were obtained on official 0.17.5 and Smart 0.17.4. Core compatibility on 0.17.6 passed (15/15) and the 32-case Web suite was re-run on R4 (official 31 PASS + 1 BLOCKED; Smart 0.17.4 30 PASS + 1 FAIL + 1 BLOCKED; Smart 0.17.5 31 PASS + 1 BLOCKED). N-15 on 0.17.6 is not directly comparable with R3.

Web client behaviour observed during model acceptance (not branch defects): the first Enter after a page reload can be ignored, and a message sent right after an MCP refresh triggered from another client can leave the working indicator stuck until reload (reproduced with the upstream refresh path as well).
